title: Reduce community malaria transmission through vaccination

concept.text: Vaccinate infectious human populations to reduce onward transmission and incident infections in the community. Pfs230D1 clinical studies demonstrate functional transmission-blocking signals, but these are not yet proof of community-level protection. Proposed completion test: WHO recommendation for transmission reduction, supported by a cluster-randomized endemic-area trial showing fewer incident human infections over at least two transmission seasons, with a prespecified efficacy confidence interval excluding no benefit. Test set by: WHO PPC: 'reduction of incident human infections at the community level.' Cluster design, two-season duration and statistical boundary are proposed operational criteria. Overlaps: INF-04, INF-13. Sources given: [WHO transmission-reducing vaccine PPC](https://www.who.int/tools/target-product-profile-database/item/ppc--for-vaccines-to-reduce-malaria-transmission) ; [Primary Pfs230D1 clinical trial publication](https://media.malariaworld.org/A_Vaccine_to_Block_Plasmodium_falciparum_Transmission_b57ee04012.pdf).

page.title: Malaria transmission-blocking vaccines
page.definition: A transmission-blocking malaria vaccine induces antibodies that act inside a mosquito. When a mosquito feeds on a vaccinated person carrying gametocytes, the sexual forms of the parasite, it takes up both parasites and antibodies. The antibodies inhibit parasite development in the mosquito. The intended effect is fewer infectious bites and fewer new infections among people in the community.

goal.need: Malaria caused an estimated 282 million cases and 610,000 deaths in 2024. Treating people who become ill misses those who can infect mosquitoes for months without symptoms. In one high-transmission setting in eastern Uganda, people without symptoms accounted for an estimated 94.7% of the human infectious reservoir. Vaccinating people who sustain transmission could protect their neighbours and help eliminate malaria locally. The benefit depends on reaching those people and on how long their antibodies remain effective.

statements.quote: However, if malaria vaccines are to contribute to programs for malaria elimination, they will need to have an impact on malaria transmission.
Establish the safety and efficacy of a Pfs230D1+ R21 combination vaccine.
statements.context: An objective of PfVIMT, which began on 1 March 2025.

statements.quote: Development of malaria vaccines that reduce transmission of the parasite and thereby substantially reduce the incidence of human malaria infection.
statements.context: The WHO-facilitated Malaria Vaccine Technology Roadmap sets this objective for licensed vaccines targeting P. falciparum and P. vivax by 2030.

completion.title: Vaccination reduces incident human malaria infections by reducing transmission at community level.
completion.criterion: Demonstrate that vaccination reduces the incidence of new human malaria infections by reducing transmission in the community. WHO describes a phase 3 cluster-randomised trial with active detection of infection, or a postlicensure effectiveness study measuring new infections in a representative community sample. The efficacy, duration and coverage needed depend on the intended setting.
completion.set_by: WHO, 2022 preferred product characteristics, section 2.3 and clinical-development guidance.
completion.threshold_quote: The vaccine should reduce malaria transmission, resulting in the reduction of incident human infections at the community level.
completion.basis: This is WHO's stated public-health endpoint. Mosquito-feeding activity alone does not establish fewer human infections. WHO allows a surrogate-based approval pathway but calls for subsequent community-effectiveness evaluation.

milestones.title: Antibodies from vaccinated animals reduce the mean oocyst count per mosquito by at least 80%.
milestones.criterion: At a stated antibody concentration, serum from vaccinated animals reduces the mean number of oocysts per mosquito by at least 80% relative to a control in a membrane-feeding assay. Oocysts are parasite cysts that develop on the mosquito gut wall.
milestones.set_by: Transmission-blocking vaccine research convention, stated as a functional benchmark by Bender et al. (2021) and used in Pfs25/Pvs25 assay studies.
milestones.threshold_quote: antibodies against a TBV candidate should block ≥80% of Plasmodium oocyst development

milestones.title: A malaria vaccine demonstrates tolerability and induces functional antibodies in a phase 1 human study.
milestones.criterion: A phase 1 trial in malaria-naive volunteers or the intended population demonstrates tolerability and a functional antibody response. In a membrane-feeding assay, antibodies from vaccinated participants reduce parasite development in mosquitoes relative to a control.
milestones.set_by: UNDP/World Bank/WHO TDR expert meeting report (2000), section B.3, phase I definition; applies to both parasite species.
milestones.threshold_quote: the ability of volunteers' antibodies to block infections of mosquitos in a membrane feed

milestones.title: Vaccination reduces malaria transmission from naturally infected people to mosquitoes.
milestones.criterion: A controlled direct-feeding study demonstrates reduced transmission of the parasite species under study from naturally infected vaccine recipients to mosquitoes, compared with controls. The outcome can be the proportion of feeds that infect at least one mosquito or the proportion of mosquitoes infected.
milestones.set_by: UNDP/World Bank/WHO TDR expert meeting report (2000), section B.3, phase II definition; applies to both parasite species.
milestones.threshold_quote: block the transmission of malaria from naturally infected vaccinees to mosquitos by direct feed.

milestones.title: A multicountry phase 3 trial confirms Pfs230D1 plus R21 is safe and reduces mosquito infection at ages ≥5.
milestones.criterion: In the PfVIMT multicountry phase 3 trial, confirm the safety of Pfs230D1 plus R21 in participants aged 5 years and older and demonstrate reduced transmission of P. falciparum to mosquitoes by direct skin feeding.
milestones.set_by: Global Health EDCTP3, PfVIMT project description; this published design and age threshold were specified for the P. falciparum combination vaccine.
milestones.threshold_quote: multi-country phase III trial involving participants of all ages 5 years and older, again using the direct skin feeding assay

milestones.title: A regulator approves a malaria vaccine for transmission reduction using a validated surrogate endpoint.
milestones.criterion: On the accelerated approval route, a regulator accepts a validated surrogate endpoint for reduced transmission in humans and grants approval on the condition that postapproval studies establish effectiveness. A phase 3 cluster-randomised trial measuring new human infections provides an alternative route to the community endpoint.
milestones.set_by: WHO, 2022 clinical-development guidance, Figure 2; the pathway and conditions are stated in a figure.
milestones.threshold_quote: Requires validated surrogate end-point of transmission reduction in humans, approved by regulatory authority

not_found: No published community-incidence efficacy result for a transmission-blocking malaria vaccine was identified for either parasite species through 15 November 2026.
No controlled direct-feeding efficacy result in naturally infected P. vivax vaccine recipients was identified.
No completed multicountry phase 3 efficacy result or surrogate-based regulatory approval was identified for either parasite species.
A between-group estimate of efficacy against new human infections in NCT03917654 could not be verified.
No statement opposing pursuit of transmission-blocking malaria vaccines was identified in the WHO, TDR or malERA guidance.

results.finding: Pooled serum from STAC-vaccinated mice (5 per group) reduced mean P. falciparum oocyst counts per mosquito by >80%.
results.detail: In a separate experiment, purified IgG from the STAC liposome group (6 mice) reduced mean oocyst counts by >98% at 75 µg/mL.
results.quote: Notably, at 243-fold dilution, only the STAC group retained more than 80% TRA, and had significantly higher TRA than other groups

results.finding: Pooled serum from Pvs25 mRNA–LNP-vaccinated mice (n=6 per group, blood from 5 patients) reduced mean P. vivax oocyst counts per mosquito by 100%.
results.quote:
all
samples from Pvs25 mRNA –LNP-immunized mice exhibited
complete (100%) transmission-blocking activity at 1:2 dilution.

results.finding: In the phase 1 main cohort (n=236), full-dose Pfs230D1-EPA/AS01 serum reduced mean mosquito oocyst counts by 89.3% in membrane feeding.
results.detail: The sample size is the main-cohort safety population. The 89.3% estimate was measured 12 weeks after dose 3 in the full-dose arm (95% CI, 83.7% to 95.0%).

results.finding: In Malian adults (52 full-dose, 112 controls), full-dose Pfs230D1-EPA/AS01 reduced P. falciparum–positive direct skin feeds by 76.5%.
results.detail: The prespecified primary analysis pooled the two vaccine regimens and found no reduction in mosquito infection during the first six weeks. The species-specific result covers two seasons, including an open-label booster season, and its confidence interval was unadjusted for multiplicity.
results.quote:
Speciation 
of oocysts in mosquitoes showed that Pfs/two.lintab/three.lintab/zero.lintabD/one.lintab vaccina -
tion was associated with reduced P . falciparum transmis -
sion.

results.finding: Pvs25H phase 1 trial (30 adults): the five highest-antibody sera reduced the number of infected mosquitoes by 20–30%.
results.detail: The assay combined vaccinee sera with blood from naturally infected donors. Control oocyst counts were calculated from feeds using matched pooled AB serum and pre-third-dose vaccinee serum.
results.quote: The five sera with the highest antibody levels from day 194 gave a 20–30% decrease in the number of infected mosquitoes.

results.finding: Serum from 10 vaccinated rabbits reduced mean oocyst counts by 99.6% versus pooled control serum.
results.detail: The assay used terminal serum collected 28 days after dose four. Rabbit serum made up 60 of 260 µL of the feed mixture.
results.quote:
The antisera induced by the 
vaccine induced strong activity with an average level of transmission reducing activity of 99.6% 
and the reduction in prevalence of 75.2%.

results.finding: Malian adults given full-dose Pfs230D1M-EPA/AS01 (n=56) tolerated it and showed functional antibody activity versus controls (p<0.01).
results.detail: The result comes from the earlier AS01 trial described in the protocol. The Matrix-M phase 1 study is presented as a plan.
results.quote:
Both fractional and full dose arms were found to have significantly higher TRA 
(Figure 15) (the decrease in the number of oocysts per infected mosquito) after both second and 
third vaccination, compared to control arms (p<0.01).

results.finding: Full-dose Pfs230D1M-EPA/AS01 in Malian adults showed 81.19% efficacy against positive skin feeds in year two (5,065 feeds across arms).
results.detail: Table 5 reports the preliminary efficacy estimate after the fourth dose. The sample size counts feeds across arms.

results.finding: Pfs25-vaccinated rabbit sera (8 rabbits, 40 P. falciparum test feeds) reduced mean oocyst counts per mosquito by 100% in four feeds.
results.detail: The four complete reductions occurred above 30,000 antibody ELISA units. The approximately 2,800-unit estimate for 80% reduction came from the fitted dose–response curve.
results.quote: Four data points, which showed more than 30,000 antibody units and 100% inhibition of oocyst density per mosquito, are not shown in these figures.

results.finding: Purified IgG from Pvs25-vaccinated mice reduced mean P. vivax oocyst counts per mosquito by >90% in each of 5 donor assays.
results.quote: purified IgG from female and male mice immunized with Pvs25 DNA plasmid significantly reduced oocyst numbers in all 5 DMFAs using different donors (>90% TRA) as compared to NMS IgG negative controls.

results.finding: Pvs25 serum from 10 rhesus macaques yielded a fitted 80% reduction in mean P. vivax oocysts per mosquito.
results.detail: Each serum sample was tested in at least three successful feeds with parasites from different patients. The concentration-response fit had an R² of 0.249.
results.quote: Based on the fitted hyperbolic curve, 50 and 80% inhibitions were achieved with approximately 1,500 and 6,000 antibody units, respectively.

results.finding: Pvs25-IMX313/Matrix-M (n=24) was well tolerated. Antibodies from most participants significantly reduced P. vivax infections in mosquitoes in preliminary assays.
results.detail: The feeding experiments were ongoing. The source gives the overall enrollment but leaves the assay sample size, effect size, and control unspecified.
results.quote: Mosquito feeding experiments are still ongoing but in the initial results, antibodies from the majority of trial participants were able to significantly reduce the number of mosquitoes becoming infected upon feeding on P. vivax infected blood.

results.finding: Pfs230D1-EPA/AS01 in school-aged children (sample size unstated) reduced the proportion of mosquitoes infected with P. falciparum by 86.4%.
results.detail: The estimate applies to Pfs230D1-EPA/AS01. The slides discuss the combination with R21 as a separate development program.
results.quote: Proportion of infected mosquitoes reduced by 86.4%

definition = "A transmission-blocking malaria vaccine induces antibodies that act inside a mosquito. When a mosquito feeds on a vaccinated person carrying gametocytes, the sexual forms of the parasite, it takes up both parasites and antibodies. The antibodies inhibit parasite development in the mosquito. The intended effect is fewer infectious bites and fewer new infections among people in the community.". Reason: The current definition presents the reduction in human infections as established, although the reported efficacy signal concerns mosquito infections.

goal.need = "Malaria caused an estimated 282 million cases and 610,000 deaths in 2024. Treating people who become ill misses those who can infect mosquitoes for months without symptoms. In one high-transmission setting in eastern Uganda, people without symptoms accounted for an estimated 94.7% of the human infectious reservoir. Vaccinating people who sustain transmission could protect their neighbours and help eliminate malaria locally. The benefit depends on reaching those people and on how long their antibodies remain effective.". Reason: The year-to-year increase alone gives neither the scale of malaria nor the reason that treating people who become ill leaves transmission unchecked.

add statement by Malaria Vaccine Funders Group, 2013: "Development of malaria vaccines that reduce transmission of the parasite and thereby substantially reduce the incidence of human malaria infection.". Reason: The Funders Group’s own wording identifies the human-infection objective behind the later CDC summary.

edit completion: criterion = "Demonstrate that vaccination reduces the incidence of new human malaria infections by reducing transmission in the community. WHO describes a phase 3 cluster-randomised trial with active detection of infection, or a postlicensure effectiveness study measuring new infections in a representative community sample. Reason: WHO specifies active detection of new infections and allows a representative community sample in postlicensure studies, two details that distinguish this endpoint from counts of patients who seek care.
